title: refactor(metadata-protocol): move the registry materialize/strip pair out of protocol.ts into protocol-registry-materialize.ts (#25467 cut 11)
body:

_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X1aK1TeYpi6AVkN7j6eFxUU)_

Part of #25467
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: 6270097840

Cut 11 of the `protocol.ts` split (#24586 ruling A, recorded in `6270097840`). Cuts 1–10 landed as #25494, #25518, #25538, #25589, #25601, #25623, #25642, #25719, #25731 and #25740. The claim is `6397346543`; the scope is the registry materialize/strip group the cut 10 report (`6393303455`) proposed from Release `6385903828`, as the server seat approved it in its dispatch order.

Four `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` members move unedited into a new module, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-materialize.ts` (#23050 shape B, one `engine` getter). `protocol.ts` loses 22 net lines (29,791 to 29,769). The cut is move-only, and the card stays open for later cuts.

Branch `claude/project-thread-f0qmfa` is the harness-pinned branch for this thread. It names no issue, so the claim comment is the identity record. It holds one commit, `f081d777`, on `main` `0790d0a469` (cut 10's merge `2c86039515` is in its history).

**Serial with the file's in-flight PRs.** Measured just before this PR was opened: none of the 12 open PRs touches `packages/metadata-protocol/src/` (each file list read in full; the release PR #25640's 226 files include the package's `CHANGELOG.md` and `package.json` only). `git log 0790d0a469..origin/main` is empty at that moment.

## What moves

| Member | Base line | Visibility | AST tokens (type params + params + return + body) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `materializeFromRegistry` | `:9071` | private | 119 |
| `governServedObject` | `:9109` | private | 28 |
| `stripMaterializedFromRegistry` | `:9134` | private | 119 |
| `stripServedObjectColumns` | `:9165` | private | 28 |

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cuts 1–10 apply it)

- **The class keeps every member** with its name, docblock, signature and position. Each body is now one host literal plus a `.call`, marked `[#25467 cut 11]`.
- **Typing.** `RegistryMaterializeHost` types every member as the class member itself (an indexed access on `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`). Each moved function keeps the method's type parameter `T` and types its `this` as the `Pick` of the host over exactly the members its body reads. Each stub annotates its literal as `ThisParameterType` of `typeof fn`. No cast, and no member changes visibility.
- **One new spelling, forced by the generics.** The four members are generic (`T` in, `T` out). `Function.prototype.call` on a generic function erases `T` to `unknown`, which `tsc` rejects against the method's declared `T` return (TS2322). So each stub instantiates the function first: the stub calls `.call` on the parenthesised instantiation expression of the function at `T` (`tsc` refuses an instantiation expression followed directly by a property access, TS1477, hence the parentheses). The emitted JavaScript is a plain `.call(host, …)`; cuts 1–10 moved no generic member, so no earlier cut needed it.
- **Members read.** `materializeFromRegistry` and `stripMaterializedFromRegistry` read the field `engine`, handed over as a GETTER so the read happens when the body makes it (tests replace `engine` on a constructed protocol). `governServedObject` calls `materializeFromRegistry` and `stripServedObjectColumns` calls `stripMaterializedFromRegistry`, each through a late-bound closure on the protocol. No private-static member, and nothing on the Release's stay list. **The order's hypothesis holds.**
- **Every other caller still calls the class method**: the five `governServedObject` read exits (one in `readFlattenedMetaItems`, three in `readMetaItem`, one on `getMetaItemLayered`'s effective layer) and the one `stripServedObjectColumns` write site in `saveMetaItem`.

## Module-level declarations, by reader

- **Two gain `export`, none moves.** The bodies read three module-level functions of `protocol.ts`: `canonicalMetaType` (already exported), and `governServedItem` and `stripServedSystemColumns`, which gain `export` in place, as cut 8 exported `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` and `runtimeHookWithoutBodyRefusal`. The new module imports all three from `protocol.js`; the cycle is evaluation-safe because each is read only inside a function body. `index.ts` names what it publishes from `protocol.ts` one by one, so the published surface does not move (measured below).
- **Measured, not assumed:** after the move, the two exported helpers have no caller left in `protocol.ts`; the moved bodies were their only callers at base too. They stay there because the class's read and write paths cite them by name in prose (for example the `getMetaItemLayered` comment on why `governServedItem` never runs on `overlay`). Moving them is noted below, not done here.
- **Imports in `protocol.ts`.** No import loses its last reader. The one new statement is the import of the new module.

## The published `.d.ts`

The series bar is ruling `6348891160`, sorted-union identity, measured first. Base `0790d0a469` and head `f081d777` were built with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol build` against one dependency tree (the closure built once at head, then the package's `src/` swapped tree-only to base for the base build and restored from `HEAD` under a trap; `git diff HEAD` empty and `git status` clean after, both blobs equal to `HEAD`'s).

- **Raw sha256**: `325970c1661efaa6a3762ce7de9e6bb205ea16099784f2b6c5950d62d175b331` at base and at head, on both `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.cts`, 772,838 bytes each (the hash cuts 8–10 reported). `cmp` exits 0 on both pairs. **Raw identity holds**, so sorted-union identity holds too. The four members are private, so each stays a `private NAME;` line.
- **Normalised sha256**: `9562749edf7b8bba67ed2f1779799a68b3d6934a8605074934572d9507c55ba6` at both ends (109 string-literal union runs sorted; this run's own normaliser).
- **The two builds differ where they should**: `index.js` hashes `b99c5148b08d3fc5…` at base (cut 10's head hash) and `bbe1a227b80604e0…` at head; the four functions' `.call(` sites occur 0 times in the base bundles and 4 times in the head bundles (ESM and CJS alike).
- **Positive control** on the head tree (on disk, restored from `HEAD` under a trap, hash equal to `HEAD`'s after): `private` dropped from `stripServedObjectColumns` and the package rebuilt. Both `.d.ts` files move to `06884ae21a4b72b4…` and print the member's full generic signature (type parameter `T`, then `(type: string, item: T): T;`), so the bar can see a change on this member.
- **Export tables.** The ESM and CJS bundles, loaded at runtime from the package, each export the same 78 names at base and head; the sorted list hashes to `9f18a0177ac736ed…` on all four. None of the moved functions, the two newly exported helpers or the host type appears.

No changeset: `skip-changeset`, per ruling `6348891160`.

## Proof of move-only

- **Bodies, by AST token** (the TypeScript compiler's AST leaf tokens, JSDoc skipped, over type parameters, parameters less the added `this`, return type and body): 294 tokens compared, **0 differ**. The type-parameter, parameter, return-type and body text, comments included, is also equal with whitespace collapsed, for all four. Negative control: one changed token in `stripMaterializedFromRegistry`'s body (`item === null` to `item !== null`, on a copy) makes the check report `differ=1`.
- **Class side.** 299 members at base and at head, in the same order. The 295 that did not move are byte-identical to base, leading comments included. Each of the 4 stubs sits at its base position and keeps its docblock and signature byte-identical.
- **Top level of `protocol.ts`.** 236 of the 238 base statements other than the class are byte-identical, leading comments included. The other two are `governServedItem` and `stripServedSystemColumns`, which gain the `export` keyword and nothing else. Head adds one statement, the new module's import.
- **Size.** +165 / −53 over 2 files, 218 changed lines. `protocol-registry-materialize.ts` has 134 lines.

## Readers of the moved lines

Every test and script that reads `protocol.ts` by path, and every test file in `packages/` and `scripts/`, was grepped for the four member names, for `governServedItem` and `stripServedSystemColumns`, and for the four registry seam names the bodies call (`materializeServedObjectOnto`, `provisionSearchCompanionOnto`, `stripMaterializedStampsFrom`, `stripProvisionedSearchCompanionFrom`).

- **No by-path reader.** Outside `protocol.ts` the member names occur only in prose: `metadata-diagnostics.ts` (a comment naming `governServedObject`'s docblock), two `CHANGELOG.md` entries, and comments in `packages/objectql` and `packages/rest` tests. No gate, baseline or ADR anchor names them.
- **The partial-registry-double fallbacks.** Six test files name the seam methods: `packages/objectql/src/protocol-meta-effective-schema.test.ts`, `registry-deployment-platform-global.test.ts`, `registry-tenant-index-author-declared-column.test.ts`, `registry-tenant-index-follows-wall.test.ts`, `meta-object-primary-designation-roundtrip.test.ts`, and `packages/rest/src/meta-object-materialization-agreement.test.ts`. Each builds the protocol over a REAL `SchemaRegistry` (which defines all four seam methods, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`) or calls the registry directly; none reads `protocol.ts` by path, and none builds a double that answers only the narrower `provisionSearchCompanionOnto` / `stripProvisionedSearchCompanionFrom` spelling. Verdict: the fallback arms move verbatim and no in-repo test reaches them (see Acceptance notes). At head, those six files plus `meta-object-search-companion-roundtrip.test.ts` pass: objectql 6 files / 57 tests, rest 1 file / 12 tests, each `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- **Bracketed-refusal pin** (`PRODUCERS`): no row owed. The four bodies hold no `new Error(` (0 by count in base lines 9032–9167); `protocol.ts` keeps its 74 such sites.
- **ADR anchors and decision letters.** `check-adr-anchors` exits 0 at both ends with **identical output**: 85 anchored files, 52,707 citations across 6,638 files, **1,846 → 1,846** decision-letter citations. The `protocol.ts` anchor file names none of the four members, and the moved bodies are not the mechanism of any entry paragraph, so the new module gets no entry.
- **Durability checker** (`check-durability-degradation-log-level --list`): identical at both ends once `[@:][0-9]+` is stripped (159 lines). The gate exits 0 at both ends with identical output. The moved `try`/`catch` arms wrap registry seam calls, not storage reads, so neither rule reads them.
- **Engine-double contract** (`check-engine-double-contract`): exits 0 at both ends. The `updateData`/`deleteData` seams keep their entries at new line numbers (14044 → 14022, 14069 → 14047). `productionFiles` is 3,690 at base and 3,692 at head: +1 is the new file, +1 is the gitignored `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`, which the spec build writes in the head tree and the clean base tree had not built.
- **Identical output at both ends:** `check-adr-symbol-anchors`, `check-system-context-census`, `check-tenant-audit-census`, `check-query-options-erasure-ratchet`, `check-filter-alias-parity`. `check-nul-bytes` differs only in the scanned file count, +1. The base-end readings were taken in a clean detached worktree at `0790d0a469`.
- **Platform checklist.** `check-platform-checklist --changed-from origin/main`: OK, 29 anchors judged, 0 lost.
- **Governed surface.** `check-governed-merges --branch claude/project-thread-f0qmfa`: 0 of 2 paths hit the register, NOT governed; 218 changed lines, under the 3,000-line human-merge bar.

## Verification

All at head `f081d777`.

- `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/metadata-protocol` exits 0. `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` on the two changed files exits 0, no output.
- **`packages/metadata-protocol` suite**, base and head, compared per test name and status (vitest `--maxWorkers=2`, JSON reporter, each run under the shared verify lock, `VERDICT command-exit 0` both legs):
  - Base `0790d0a469`: 21,509 tests (21,490 passed, 0 failed, 19 skipped), 266 files.
  - Head `f081d777`: 21,509 tests (21,490 passed, 0 failed, 19 skipped), 266 files.
  - None lost, none changed status, none added. The base leg is the package `src/` swapped tree-only from `0790d0a469` (the new module removed from the tree) and restored from `HEAD` under a trap.
- **Derived gates.** `dispatch-gates --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 53 gates on 2 changed paths; all 53 exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:lean-entry-closure` first answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3, unbuilt `dist/`) and exit 0 after a full `pnpm build` (76/76 tasks, `VERDICT command-exit 0`); the plugin-teardown fixture commit was fetched before the first run. `dispatch-gates --ran`: 53 derived, 53 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN, exit 0.

## Acceptance notes

- The fallback arms of `materializeFromRegistry` and `stripMaterializedFromRegistry` (the narrower `provisionSearchCompanionOnto` / `stripProvisionedSearchCompanionFrom` spellings for partial registry doubles) are reached by no test in this repository: every protocol in the six named test files is built over a real `SchemaRegistry`, which answers the wider seam first. They move verbatim; whether to keep them is not this cut's question. Not class a/b/c.
- `governServedItem` and `stripServedSystemColumns` now have their only callers in `protocol-registry-materialize.ts`. A later cut could move them there; it would re-point the `{@link}` references in the class docblocks and the prose comments that name them.

## Carry-forward

Unchanged from cut 10: public members whose return type is inferred, the bodies kept by a reader (`probeRecord`, `getMetaItemCached`, `findReferencesToMeta`, `packagelessAddress`, `refuseUnmintableMetaType`, `metaTypeNamespaceExists`, `viewContainerNameCollisionRefusal` with `overlaidShippedContainerViewNames`, `reportPageRequiresAbsentAtLoad`, the 7 `applyRegistryWriteThrough` callers, `readCodeLayerForCarryForward`), and the private-static readers stay in `protocol.ts`.
